versions.content: The part <NAME> from [SWS_MemMap_00022] shall con- tain the following core scope keywords to indicate the restriction/qualifications: {coreScope} = • GLOBAL is code/data which can be executed/accessed by any core in case of multi-core ECUs. • LOCAL code/data must be mapped by the integrator to a specific core (Core 0, Core 1, ...) in case of multi-core ECUs. The {coreScope} tag can be considered optional in case it is GLOBAL . Means in case no {coreScope} keyword is added the default shall be treated as GLOBAL . Instead the {coreScope} tag LOCAL shall be considered as mandatory. Background: Scope of LOCAL SwAddrMethod is visible and can not be mixed up with GLOBAL SwAddrMethods.

versions.content: The part <NAME> from [SWS_MemMap_00022] shall contain the following {coreScope} keywords with the values GLOBAL as optional default without restrictions in memory access and LOCAL as mandatory alternative setting with restrictions in memory access to one desired core. Consequently, the {coreScope} value GLOBAL shall not be written in the MAKW as well as SwAddrMethod name. The usage of {coreScope} LOCAL is limited to the section types it is specified for. In addition for section types VAR , VAR_FAST , VAR_SLOW , INTERNAL_VAR the usage of {coreScope} is only permitted for {INIT_POLICY} equal to CLEARED or INIT . This restriction shall reduce the complexity of memory layouts and reduce the amount of memory holes due to typical allocation restrictions valid for non initialized memory sections.
